scope: Seven exposed development positions; normal30s final reliability and preservation run.

cases.source: 100 Endgame Patterns, personal reading PDF page60, Zamarbide-Benitez La Roda2005, White35g4? versus35Ke3!, diagram visually checked.
cases.history_limit: The diagram fixes the board and side. Earlier history and halfmove clock are unavailable; use zero for this research start, no repetition or fifty-move inference.
cases.human_task: Test whether immediately spending g3-g4 allows ...f6 and a king blockade, while Ke3 preserves g4 as a later waiting move to gain f5. The move order must matter against the opponent best replies, not only the book line.
falsifiers: If g4 still wins, reject the lost-win hypothesis.
If Ke3 does not win in bounded searches, do not assume the book judgment is proven.
Do not call one PV forced or equate a pawn-count difference with the waiting-move mechanism.

cases.source: John Doknjas, Opening Repertoire The Modern Benoni, PDF pages59-60 (printed58-59), Game7 variation12Nd2?!; successor12...Nb6 diagram visually checked.
cases.human_task: Nd2 supports e4 but withdraws the active f3 knight. Test whether ...Nb6 and the threat ...Nfxd5 make this natural defence inferior to Re1; explain the concrete enabled response and its cost.
falsifiers: Do not claim ...Nb6 forces material gain from one PV.
The queen on c2 and bishop on e2 must be tracked; an attack count is not a proof of an unanswerable threat.
If modern equal-depth analysis does not separate the alternatives, report the book hypothesis as unconfirmed.

cases.source: 100 Endgame Patterns personal reading edition, PDF59 reserve tempi series, position1. Diagram visually checked.
cases.human_task: The book uses a3 to make the black king move, then Ke5 and f5. Test the early f5 break. Capture-induced king entry can differ from a quiet king retreat; record missing coverage rather than change the rule after seeing output.
cases.history_limit: Earlier game history unavailable; zero clocks cannot support repetition or fifty-move claims.

cases.source: 100 Endgame Patterns personal reading edition, PDF page 51, Kharlov-Ernst, Haninge 1992, 47...g5? versus drawing king moves. Diagram visually checked.
cases.human_task: The immediate opposing g4 counterbreak creates separated passed pawns. Explain that response if verified. Keeping a pawn move is not itself a complete account of this error.
falsifiers: If no important difference is established between g5 and legal king choices, do not import the book loss into the product result.
Do not replace the actual g4 counterbreak with an unrelated king waiting route.
The later passed-pawn captures and promotions must remain attached to their actual branches.

cases.mainline_san: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3 Nf6 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O c6 Qc2 b6 Nbd2 Bb7 e4
cases.human_task: Judge a routine developing move by whether it gives White an effective central advance and leaves Black unable to challenge the wedge in time.
cases.hypothesis: After Nbd7, e5 gains time against Nf6, closes Bb7 and leaves weaker central counterplay than Na6 followed by c5. Test each link separately.
falsifiers: e5 is legal after both moves: legality alone proves no timing difference.
A strong response after Nbd7 challenges the centre comparably.
Na6 does not improve the relevant central response or the engine rejects the book preference.

source.diagram: PDF8 upper left after Nbd7 visually checked

cases.human_task: Explain the first checking reply and lost queen-capture opportunity with their consequences.
cases.hypothesis: Moving the f1 rook permits a dangerous Qf2+ reply; the alternative captures the queen and pays the rook.
falsifiers: Qf2 is already equally effective against the alternative.
The stated follow-up can be avoided by an adequate tested defense.

cases.source: 100 Endgame Patterns personal reading edition, PDF page 52, Simic-Nikolic, Vrsac 1981, 44...g5? versus 44...f5. Diagram visually checked.
cases.human_task: The same g4 counterbreak can create a distant h-passer, but this board also has blocked a- and c-pawns and a white e-pawn. Test the actual defensive choices. The book has both ...hxg4 h5 and ...f5 gxh5; neither exact line is supplied to the product.
falsifiers: If the same counterbreak works just as well after the alternative, reject the changed-reply explanation.
A passed h-pawn is not by itself proof of a win: the race, checks and relevant pawn prices must stay correctly scoped.
Do not count a later waiting-move anecdote as explaining the immediate counterbreak.
cases.history_limit: The written prefix is replayed; earlier history is unavailable. Initial zero halfmove clock is not repetition or fifty-move evidence.
